title: How to Fix Cracks in Drywall
metaDescription: Hairline or corner cracks showing up in your walls or ceiling? Here's how to fix them so they don't just come back in a few months.
symptom: Thin cracks in a wall or ceiling, often near corners, door frames, or where a wall meets the ceiling.
estimatedTime: 1-2 hours active work, plus drying time between coats

steps.heading: Widen the crack slightly
steps.body: Run a utility knife along the crack to open it very slightly (a V-groove) — this gives the joint compound something to actually grip instead of just sitting on top of a hairline gap that will telegraph back through.

steps.heading: Clean out dust and debris
steps.body: Brush or vacuum away any loose drywall dust from the widened crack so the compound bonds directly to solid material.

steps.heading: Apply mesh tape over the crack
steps.body: Press self-adhesive fiberglass mesh tape directly over the full length of the crack — this is the step most DIY crack fixes skip, and skipping it is why the crack usually comes back within a year. The tape bridges the crack so future minor movement doesn't reopen it.

steps.heading: Apply joint compound over the tape
steps.body: Using a putty knife, spread a thin, even layer of joint compound over the tape, feathering the edges a few inches out on both sides. Let it dry fully — usually overnight.

steps.heading: Sand and apply a second coat
steps.body: Lightly sand the first coat, then apply a second, slightly wider coat to further feather the edges into the wall for an invisible transition. Let dry again.

steps.heading: Final sand, prime, and paint
steps.body: Sand smooth, wipe away dust, prime the patched area, and paint to match the surrounding wall.

whenToCallAPro: A single crack that comes back repeatedly after proper taping, cracks wider than about 1/4 inch, or diagonal cracks at door/window corners across multiple rooms can indicate the house is settling or has a structural issue — worth having a contractor or structural engineer take a look rather than just re-patching.
safetyWarnings: Wear a dust mask when sanding dried joint compound, especially indoors with limited ventilation.
